name: 3DXTECH
summary: US engineering-filament producer based in Grand Rapids, Michigan, running a 68,000 sq ft ISO 9001:2015-certified plant. Makes everything it sells in-house, from commodity PLA/PETG up to ultra-performance PEEK, PEKK and PEI, plus carbon- and glass-filled composites, ESD-safe grades and pellets. Sub-brands cover product families rather than separate companies: Triton3D (Stratasys-compatible spools), 3DXLabs, ThermaX, CarbonX, OBSIDIAN and 3DXSTAT.

product_lines.name: Economy PLA / ECOMAX PLA
product_lines.notes: Unmodified general-purpose PLA; ECOMAX is the economy tier.

product_lines.name: 3DXTECH ABS
product_lines.notes: Generic ABS.

product_lines.name: Pellets
product_lines.notes: Raw pellets in matching chemistries for large-format machines; out of scope for a filament catalog.

additional_notes: Sells filament dryers (FD1) and filament maintainers (FM1) as accessories, plus pellets for larger-format machines; no build-plate or print-surface products were found, so makes_plates is set false on absence of evidence rather than a positive statement. Its own FAQ confirms enterprise customers run 3DXTECH material in Stratasys printers via the Triton3D line, but that is a compatibility/aftermarket play, not an OEM supply relationship with Stratasys. No evidence found that 3DXTECH white-labels for other retail brands or resells anyone else's extrusion, so oem_relationships is deliberately empty. Markets itself as a 'leading supplier of ultra-polymer 3D printing filaments' with 25+ years of parent expertise in high-performance materials. Price tier is 'engineering' overall even though its PLA/PETG/ABS sit at mid-tier pricing.

provenance.conflicts: None between sources. Two absence-of-evidence calls: no build-plate products were found (makes_plates false) and no Reddit/Discord/TikTok presence was found (likely none official, but unconfirmed).
